description: Accessibility barriers in a project's markup, each named against the WCAG 2.2 criterion a regulator would cite, with the evidence to check it. Two kinds of answer, kept apart on purpose: barriers that reading the markup proves (no alt attribute at all, a field with no label anywhere, a div that only a mouse can activate), and the ones only a person can settle, where something is written as an expression or a component and the markup cannot say. It also returns every criterion it did NOT check - contrast, focus order, whether alt text is any good - because those need a rendered page. Use it before shipping an interface, or when asked whether something is accessible; a clean result means these checks found nothing, never that the product is accessible. No browser, no network, no model.

axeReport.description: The JSON from an axe run OR a Lighthouse report, if the project has either - Lighthouse runs axe rules, so both work. It settles contrast, which reading markup cannot, and its findings are triaged rather than relayed: rules that map to no WCAG criterion are reported as advice, and what the tool could not determine becomes a question.

path.description: A file or directory inside the project to check instead of all of it

project.description: Absolute path of the project folder
